title: Descent set and being an n-cycle are asymptotically independent, uniformly over all descent sets (Elizalde–Troyka Conjecture 5.1)
source: Sergi Elizalde and Justin M. Troyka, “Exact and asymptotic enumeration of cyclic permutations according to descent set”, arXiv:1710.05103 (J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 165, 2019), Conjecture 5.1. https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05103
statement:
For each $n$, let $[n-1]=\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $\beta_n(I)$ denote the number of permutations in $S_n$ with descent set $I\subseteq[n-1]$, while $\beta^{\mathrm{cyc}}_n(I)$ denotes the number of $n$-cycles with descent set $I$. **Asymptotic independence conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\max_{\varnothing \subsetneqq I \subsetneqq [n-1]} \left| \frac{n\, \beta^{\mathrm{cyc}}_n(I)}{\beta_n(I)} - 1\right| = 0.
$$

This asserts that, uniformly over all non-empty proper descent sets, having descent set $I$ and being an $n$-cycle are asymptotically independent, with the proportion of $n$-cycles tending to $1/n$ as it does among all permutations. The source presents this as a conjectural strengthening of the known asymptotic independence result for alternating permutations.
summary: The conjecture holds. The source's own Theorem 3.1(c) writes n·β^cyc_n(I) as β_n(I) plus a signed sum, over the divisors d ≥ 2 of n, of the counts β_{n/d}(I/d) for the compressed descent sets, so everything reduces to showing that these smaller counts are negligible against β_n(I) uniformly in I. The source's bound for them is absolute and fails when β_n(I) is small. The new step is a counting inequality, β_n(I) ≥ (n^{2/3}/40)·β_{n/d}(I/d) for every divisor d ≥ 2 and every nonempty proper I: each permutation counted on the right is inflated into blocks and then modified either by swaps of disjoint free pairs (decoded by block rank sums) or by sliding a single letter along a long monotone run (at most four preimages), giving many distinct permutations with descent set I. With τ(n) ≤ 2√n this gives |n·β^cyc_n(I)/β_n(I) − 1| ≤ 80·n^{−1/6}. Lean defines β and β^cyc literally (permutations with exact descent set in one-line notation; cycles with full support), proves the counting inequality, the bound and the printed limit of the maximum, and takes Theorem 3.1(c) of the source as an explicit hypothesis.
paste_summary: Proved, using one theorem of the source. Elizalde and Troyka (arXiv:1710.05103, Conjecture 5.1) conjectured that the maximum over nonempty proper descent sets I of |n·β^cyc_n(I)/β_n(I) − 1| tends to 0. Their Theorem 3.1(c) reduces this to bounding the counts for compressed descent sets, and a new counting inequality, β_n(I) ≥ (n^{2/3}/40)·β_{n/d}(I/d), bounds them uniformly in I.
caveat: One link is outside Lean: the Lean theorems take Elizalde and Troyka's Theorem 3.1(c) (printed and proved in the source, identical in arXiv v1 to v3) as an explicit hypothesis, transcribed literally over the source's range; the final check confirmed the transcription and verified the identity exactly for every n ≤ 11 and every I (2,047 cases), so the hypothesis is not vacuous. The new mathematics is the counting inequality; the rest is the source's formula and a triangle inequality, and the argument is short and elementary. The explicit bound 80·n^{−1/6} exceeds 1 for every n up to about 2.6·10^11, so it carries no numerical content; the result is the limit, as conjectured. The journal text (JCTA 2019) was not read (reviewer's probability that it settles the conjecture: below 0.02). All work is by AI and no human has checked it: the proof, the Lean code and the paper are by GPT-6.2 Sol lanes; the adversarial review before Lean (not routine 0.70) and the final check (0.65) are by two separate Claude Opus 5.5 lanes.
